newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks break three-day losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks break three-day losing streak.

text.p: Tokyo stocks broke their three-day losing streak on Tuesday, ending higher as the yen's decline against the dollar triggered bargain-hunting of blue-chip issues, brokers said.
"As profit-taking had pulled down blue chips, such as Sony Corp, they were likely to rise back up again," said Tetsuya Ishijima, Okasan Securities' chief strategist.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 148.72 points or 0.75 percent to close at 19,853.89. The index briefly reached 19,926.79.
Shares in the banking sector were hurt by Tokai Kogyo's woes, as banks had heavily financed construction firms, which are now burdened with massive bad loans, brokers said.
By sector, decliners were led by banks, rubber, iron/steel, and nonferrous metals. Gainers were led by warehousing, trading houses, ceramics, real estate, and insurers.
The second section index finished 0.92 point lower at 1,806.16, with 7.29 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 3.35 points at 1,191.91.
